advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_MAKE_WORKFLOW_CALL` capture ALL targets in a multi-target `make` invocation (or split the trailing arg list) so no reachable recipe escapes the POSIX scan.
evidence: The regex has one `target` group and no repetition, so `make lint typecheck` matches only `lint`. A recipe reachable only as a second-or-later target on a shared `make` line is never scanned; `_make_recipe_violations` then returns empty for it — indistinguishable from 'scanned and clean'.
advisory.finding: `_MAKE_WORKFLOW_CALL` captures only a single target per `make` invocation, so a workflow step running multiple targets on one line (e.g. `make lint typecheck`) seeds only the first; the remaining targets and their transitive recipes never enter the reachable set and silently escape the POSIX-dash scan.
scenarios: A future CI step invokes several Make targets on one line; a bash-only construct in the un-seeded sibling target passes the green POSIX lane unchecked.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the case-modification regex to match doubled modifiers (`\^\^`/`,,`) as well as single ones.
evidence: `[\^,]\}` requires exactly one modifier char before `}`; `${var^^}` presents two carets, so the second breaks the `\}` anchor and the match fails.
advisory.finding: The `case-modification` non-POSIX pattern only matches a single trailing `^` or `,`, so bash's all-chars case modifiers `${var^^}` and `${var,,}` are not detected as bash-only constructs.
scenarios: A CI-reachable recipe uses `${VAR^^}` (bash upper-case-all), a construct /bin/sh does not support, and the scanner reports no violation.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Factor the shared construct-scanning loop into one helper that both `_make_recipe_violations` and `_bash_only_make_recipe_violations` call.
evidence: Both derive bodies (one via `_make_recipe_bodies(makefile_text)`, one from a pre-built dict) and apply the same patterns; only the violation string format differs.
advisory.finding: `_make_recipe_violations` and `_bash_only_make_recipe_violations` are two parallel implementations of the same non-POSIX construct scan differing only in input shape and message format, inviting divergence as the construct set evolves.
scenarios: A future edit adds a construct or fixes a pattern in one helper but not the other, so the two POSIX-parity tests disagree on what counts as a violation.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive-control assertion to `test_ci_reachable_make_recipes_stay_posix_dash_static_text` that a seeded non-POSIX construct on the transitive path is reported.
evidence: 1827-1831: asserts `not violations` only; unlike `test_ci_reachable_make_recipes_reject_bash_only_constructs` (1865-1868) it never seeds a known violation to confirm the scanner fires.
Combined with the single-target seed limitation above, an empty violations list cannot distinguish 'all reachable recipes scanned and clean' from 'a reachable recipe was never seeded/scanned'.
advisory.finding: `test_ci_reachable_make_recipes_stay_posix_dash_static_text` has no positive control proving the scan can detect a violation on the transitive/`$(MAKE)`-reachable path; it only asserts the real tree is clean, so a scan that never inspects a reachable recipe reads identically to a clean result.
scenarios: A regression drops a recipe from the reachable set; this test stays green because it lacks an inject-and-detect control.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add seeded-input assertions proving each of the four remaining _MAKE_NON_POSIX_CONSTRUCTS patterns ('[[', 'declare -a'/'arr[i]=', '<<<', '${var^}'/'${var,}') actually flags its construct, so a regex typo cannot silently disable detection.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:1651 defines five patterns: 'set -o pipefail', 'double-bracket test' (r"\[\["), 'indexed/associative array', 'here-string' (r"<<<"), 'case-modification' (r"\$\{...[\^,]\}")
tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:1866 seeded["lint"] = "\tset -o pipefail\n" + seeded["lint"]; then asserts violations == ["lint: set -o pipefail"] — the ONLY seeded construct

ABSENCE: no test seeds '[[ $x = y ]]', 'declare -a arr', 'cat <<<"$x"', or '${name^}' into a reachable recipe and asserts _make_recipe_violations / _bash_only_make_recipe_violations flags it; a broken regex for any of these four would pass every test
advisory.finding: Of the five newly added non-POSIX-dash construct patterns in _MAKE_NON_POSIX_CONSTRUCTS, only 'set -o pipefail' has a test proving the regex actually matches its intended construct (via the seeded recipe in test_ci_reachable_make_recipes_reject_bash_only_constructs). The other four patterns — double-bracket test ('[['), indexed/associative array ('declare -a foo' or 'foo[bar]='), here-string ('<<<'), and case-modification ('${var^}' / '${var,}') — are non-trivial regexes with no positive-match assertion, so a typo in any of them (e.g. an unescaped bracket or a wrong quantifier) would silently make that construct undetectable while every test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_ci_reachable_make_recipes_reject_bash_only_constructs (or a table-driven parametrization), seed each construct into a copy of a reachable recipe and assert the corresponding violation label appears, e.g. for label, snippet in [('double-bracket test', '[[ -n "$x" ]]'), ('indexed/associative array', 'declare -a arr'), ('here-string', 'cat <<<"$x"'), ('case-modification', '${x^}')]: assert any(label in v for v in _bash_only_make_recipe_violations({**recipes, 'lint': '\t' + snippet + '\n'})).
